utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The Chamber would like to start with giving a decision on a request for protective measures for Witness 21. On the 3rd of April, 2007, the Prosecution requested the Chamber to allow Witness 21 to retain his earlier granted pseudonym and as well to grant face and voice distortion. The Defence has not opposed this application. As the Court has stated on prior occasions, the party seeking protective measures for a witness must demonstrate an objectively grounded risk to the security or welfare of the witness or the witness's family, should it become known that a witness has given evidence before the Tribunal. In the present case, it appears that the witness has received threatening telephone calls in attempt to prevent him from testifying in this court. Moreover, the witness's close family has suffered damage to property and the witness has had problems with his employment situation, possibly due to his imminent testimony. The witness's family is still resident in the region. These indications fulfil the Chamber's requirements for grants of protective measures. The Chamber therefore grants the request for pseudonym and face and voice distortion. This concludes the reasons for the Chamber's decision on protective measures for Witness 21. And Mr. Dutertre, are you the one who will deal with Witness 21?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And are you ready to call Witness 21?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed, Your Honour. With an indication, if I may. We have prepared for part of his testimony a consolidated document. We would like to submit this document to the Court according to Rule 92 ter. The witness will be here. Cross-examination will be carried out, and the Chamber will also be free to ask questions, and he will be able to confirm that his testimony will reflect his statement. I've also prepared a short summary of this consolidated statement, and if you agree, of course, after we've confirmed identity details in closed session I will be in a position in open session to read this brief statement. And then I could start with the examination-in-chief of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Has the Defence received a copy of the consolidated statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have. There is no objection to the Court's proposed subject to this, at least as far as the Haradinaj Defence team is concerned that is the position. We would respectfully request that the summary, if it is to be read into the record, be read into the record in the absence of the witness rather than in his presence and translated to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I -- the purpose of reading it into the record is mainly to inform the public about it, not to remind the witness of what in summary his evidence is. Mr. Dutertre, you would agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then as far as the other Defence teams are concerned. Mr. Guy-Smith, any objection any against introduction through 92 ter?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then, Mr. Dutertre, you may proceed as you suggested. Therefore, then, I think it would be best then to start with the summary to inform the public that later when the witness appears no further questions will be put to him in relation to what is in his statement, a statement which is, I take it, to be admitted under seal due to the protective measures, and that therefore I also take it that the summary -- that you have taken into account that the summary does not reveal any identifying elements. Then, please proceed before we ask the usher to bring the witness in, but perhaps the usher could already prepare for that situation. Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed. Thank you very much, Your Honour. This consolidated witness statement which was sent to the Chamber yesterday has also annexes and it will be tendered under seal to protect the identity of Witness 21. We've also redacted as much as possible identity details in the brief summary, i.e., the names of victims are kept, but we've tried not to mention the existing links. I'd like to read in English this brief summary. [In English] "Witness 21 is a Catholic Albanian male. In 1998 he was living near Djakovica in Kosovo. "Illira and Tush Frrokaj went missing in KLA territory sometime in August 1998. They were both Catholic Albanians, and both lived in Pljancor. "The witness last saw them in the house in Pljancor on the morning of the day they left Pljancor for Nepole, Peje municipality. He was told they had left later that day to visit Illira's sister in Nepole. Tush's mother said they left in the family car, a dark red Opel Kadett. "The safest route through KLA-controlled area to Nepole in 1998 was from Pljancor through Dujak, Gramaqel, Dubrave, Gllogjan, Rznic, and Ratis. "Tush's mother reported late that night that Tush and Illira had not yet returned. The family waited until after midday the next day and reported their disappearance was reported to the Djakovica police. The police said that they had not detained Tush and Illira Frrokaj nor was there a report of their car having been in an accident. "Tush's brother-in-law reported that Illira and Tush never arrived in Nepole. "Two days after Tush and Illira disappeared, a Roma confirmed that he had seen Tush and Illira driving from Pljancor on the asphalt road turning right towards Dujak in the early afternoon the day they went missing. "The witness then travelled with two other of the -- to the first KLA check-point at the entry to Gramaqel village. "Five KLA soldiers were present at the check-point in Gramaqel. Two soldiers explained to Witness 21 that they had been present along with two other KLA soldiers when Tush and Illira had passed through the check-point. They allowed Tush and Illira through, but advised Tush against driving through. "One of those went with Witness 21 on to Gllogjan. He told the witness that the KLA soldiers at the entry check-point told him that a red Kadett had passed through after Balaj questioned the occupants. "This person then travelled to the Gllogjan exit check-point where KLA soldiers told him that the car had not passed through that check-point. "The following days, the fourth or fifth days after Tush's and Illira's disappearance onwards, Witness 21 and that person went back to the entry and exit check-points in Gllogjan. The witness spoke on different days to different KLA soldiers at the check-points. The soldiers repeated what they had earlier told the other person about Balaj interrogating the occupants of the Kadett for half an hour at the entry-point to Gllogjan. The witness also heard from the guards at the exit check-point to Gllogjan that Tush and Illira never passed that check-point. "The following day the witness heard that there were -- that there were two bodies in the Lake Radonjic canal area. "He then went with another person to KLA headquarters in Gllogjan. Witness 21 met Ramush Haradinaj's brother Shkelzen, who asked for Tush and Illira's photograph and said the KLA would search for them. Shkelzen then gave him a handwritten authorising to travel in the Dukagjin zone. "The witness then went with the other person to the canal, where the other pointed out the dead bodies. "The witness did not know Idriz Balaj. He met him twice in his search for Tush and Illira, but Balaj refused to speak to him." [Interpretation] This concludes the reading of the summary, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Three brief matters, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: First of all, just to make it absolutely clear, it's obviously the position the Prosecution does not intend to elicit that evidence in chief from the witness, but it is the intention of the Defence to ask questions arising from that statement in that account in the course of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's understood.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Secondly, there was an error in the reading out of the summary which is of some material significance. Page 5, line 7 of the transcript is -- was a misreading of the first sentence of paragraph 10 of the written summary. Paragraph 10 of the written summary records that one of those who had been, that is one of those with Witness 21, then went to Gllogjan, whereas paragraph -- page 5, line 7, records one of those went with Witness 21 to Gllogjan. The important distinction is, and as I understand it this reflects the evidence, Witness 21 was not with the person who went to Gllogjan to make those inquiries. That is accurately reflected in the written summary, but is inaccurately reflected in the misreading of that sentence on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see Mr. Dutertre nodding yes, so it seems that he agrees.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... point Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And finally, paragraph 15 of the written summary, the witness then went with the other person to the canal, where the other pointed out the dead bodies, is not reflected in the 92 bis statement; in other words, that passage is not part of the 92 bis statement, which ceases just before that part of the chronology.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unless I'm mistaken, Your Honour, I've just checked. In paragraph 57 of such consolidated statement, it is indicated, this particular fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I apologise and withdraw that third point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's then all clarified. Mr. Dutertre, are you prepared to call the first -- yes, I take it that you'll start by asking the witness to confirm his statement. Are you ready to have the witness be brought into the courtroom? Madam Registrar, I see that the curtains are down. Face and voice distortion are in place. Mr. Dutertre, may I take it that you have fully explained to the witness the procedure of 92 ter so that he's familiar with it? Thank you. Is the consolidated statement in the hands of the registry yet or not? Perhaps we could already distribute it since there seems -- or is it uploaded?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It has not been given to the registry yet. I have a copy, but not a colour copy, for the registry and for the parties. Maybe we could just show the document, and then we will give to the registry the final document with colour copies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Good afternoon, Witness 21. You are looking around who's speaking to you; it's me, Witness 21. The Chamber has decided that you'll testify under a pseudonym. That's the reason why I call you Witness 21 and why I do not use your name. And that face distortion and voice distortion will be applied. That means outside of this courtroom one cannot see your face, one cannot hear your voice, although the content of your testimony is public. Before you give evidence, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text is now handed out to you by the usher. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you -- the interpreters could not hear you. Could you perhaps come a bit closer to that microphone and repeat the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness 21. Please be seated. Witness 21, you'll first be examined by Mr. Dutertre, who's counsel for the Prosecution. Mr. Dutertre, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Are we still in closed session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are in open session. Yes, but face distortion, voice distortion, and pseudonym, and since the curtains are down, those, if there would be anyone in the public gallery, would not be able to see the face of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was just asking to know whether I would have to ask the witness about all identity details to get a confirmation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it's just a matter of name and date of birth, you can do it by showing him a pseudonym sheet. If you want to go into further details, you have to apply for private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like 65 ter 1219. This, obviously, should not be shown to the public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the pseudonym sheet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Madam -- Witness 21, would you -- it's under seal. Witness 21, would you look at your screen where you will see something appear soon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is there something on the screen or what?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not yet, if you wait for a second. There seems to be -- Madam Registrar, is there any problem in producing the document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it remains problematic, perhaps we could work with a hard copy; but if it's ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I suggest that I could put the name on a piece of paper by hand. Unfortunately, it says something on the back of this piece of paper, but we could ask the witness not to look at what it says and simply confirm that this is, in fact, his first name and last name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But then of course we would need that piece of paper at a later stage. So if there's something written on the back, it might not be the --

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall take another piece of paper then, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could we at the same time check that we do not have similar problems? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness 21, you have before you a sheet of paper. It says something on that piece of paper. Could you tell us whether what's written on that piece of paper is, in fact, your name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could the piece of paper then be shown to the Defence and then to the Bench. I suggest that a number will be assigned to this piece of paper, but I leave open the possibility to have this one replaced by an electronic version. Madam Registrar, that would be number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number P41.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Witness 21, do you remember having met me last week?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Do you remember having made a statement on a part of your witness statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Witness 21, I'm now about to show you a copy of a document, and you will tell me whether this is, in fact, what you stated last week on part of what you know about this business. This document includes a main part and some additions.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: Yes, this is it. These are the statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Witness, could you perhaps be more specific and tell us whether this is an exact expression of your statement, in fact, what you would say right now if I were to ask you questions about the various subjects brought up in -- on this paper?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Madam Registrar -- I don't think the witness would need his statement at this moment. So, Madam Usher, could you please get the statement from the witness, give it to Madam Registrar, so that she can assign a number to it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number P42, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And under seal, I take it, Madam Registrar. Please proceed, Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Witness 21, we are going to carry on starting at the end of this written testimony. I'm going to ask you questions specifically about this part. Witness 21, we know that the canal Radonjic is for part made out of concrete, another part is natural. Could you tell us exactly at which place on the canal you went the first time that you visited the canal.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: The first time we went to the canal following the Gllogjan road from Ratishe to Gllogjan. We turned right, and before we got to the farm we turned left where the concrete canal divides from the natural canal. When we went there, we saw two bodies in the canal.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you for these clarifications. Let's take things in stages. Do you remember having gone to canal Radonjic in January 2007 with Barney Kelly and myself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Do you remember that Mr. Kelly took pictures that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to show Exhibit 61 ter 992, page 14 -- 65 ter 992, page 14.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we have one button at the top which you can make negative or positive, I think. There we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Witness 21, what do you see on this picture?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: This photo shows where the concrete canal ends and the natural canal begins.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Just a few questions so we can find our way. If you follow the canal towards the left, meaning up, where does that take you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: If you go left, the -- that takes you to Ratishe. If you go down, then that leads you Radoniq, to the lake.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: On this photograph, where would the village of Gllogjan be, to the right of the canal or to the left? I understand that we don't see the village on the picture. I just want to know which side it would be on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: It would be on the left of the canal.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: You have a pen in front of you. Could you draw an arrow pointing in the direction of Gllogjan and put a G next to it to show Gllogjan.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we see on this picture the actual spot that you went to that day in August 1998, the first time you visited the canal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: Yes, it's the same canal here. This is where I was, in this part here. Would you like me to mark it?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Yes, please. Mark it with a letter --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: Right here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Perhaps with a cross and the letter A, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Now, once you were at the canal, what did you see? You told us two bodies.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: When did you see these bodies -- where were you exactly when you saw these bodies? From which spot did you actually see them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: I was at the letter A, where I marked letter A. That's where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to keep this picture as it stands, stating that this is a picture taken in 2007, and since then there have been -- there's been renovation work, which is visible on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just to be absolutely clear, the renovation work had taken place before these photographs were taken rather than since, and I think Mr. Dutertre was intending to convey that, but lest Your Honours should be misunderstood. And we can see in this series of photographs that there had been some reconstruction going on. It doesn't affect the structure of the photograph you are looking at at the moment, but the reconstruction had already begun by the time these photographs were taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is very, very -- exactly what I meant to say. When the picture was taken, the work -- the renovation work was not finished, so you see things on this picture that were not there in 1998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for that clarification. Mr. Dutertre, do I understand that you only want to have the marked photograph as an exhibit? Yes. Madam Registrar, that would then be number ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number P43, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. And there's no need to have this under seal, Mr. Dutertre or -- this will be public. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Witness 21, where were the two bodies that you mentioned when you went to the canal? Where were they exactly located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: They were inside the water, in the canal.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to see evidence 65 ter 992, page 17. I was asking for number 17. I think that what we see now is number 24.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, if you had followed that, it seems that number 24 is on the screen now, whereas Mr. Dutertre asked for number 17.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Witness 21, what is on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: The photo shows the canal, the new part that is being constructed, and then the old part where it used to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Could you show with two arrows the -- on this photograph the part where we have the beginning of the natural part of the canal in 1998.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Could you indicate this with a letter A next to the arrow.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Witness 21, if it's visible on this photo, could you indicate the position where you saw the two bodies in 1998 the first time that you went to the canal.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: I can show you approximately where they were. I think this part here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Could you indicate this with a letter B, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to retain this, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the marked copy of photo 17 would be number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number P44, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. No need to have it under seal, Mr. Dutertre, I take it?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Witness 21, could you describe the bodies that you saw on that day.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: That day when I went there to see the bodies, when I saw the bodies, they were face-down and they were swollen. And as far as I could see, the man had a black T-shirt, jeans, and black socks, while the woman had a track-suit and T-shirt and, I think, red sandals. I did not know them, who they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Were the bodies in their entire state?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: Yes, they were whole bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Did you see clothing that could have been military clothing or was it just civilian clothing that they had on them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: As far as I remember, they were not wearing military clothes. They just had this T-shirt, black T-shirt, the male, and track-suit. I did not see military clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: If you saw any signs of violence on those bodies, what were these signs of violence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: I did not see any signs of violence, just the bullet-holes, that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Where did you see the bullet-holes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: On their backs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: In general, what was the weather like? Was there a lot of rain? A little rain? No rain at all? What is your recollection of the weather conditions on that day in 1998?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: What about the water in the canal on your first visit, was there a lot of water going through the canal? Was there little water? How would you describe it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: I don't think there was lots of water flowing. There was not even little water flowing. It was an average amount of water.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Were the bodies moving in the water because of the flow of the water or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: No. The bodies were stuck in a part on the right side.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: When you say "stuck," could you explain precisely what you mean when you say that they were stuck on the right side.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: They were in the water, but they had stopped. They were not flowing together with the water. They had -- the bodies had stopped on the side of the canal, on this side of the canal.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: They were stuck by what, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: If you can see the B letter that I marked, it's there that they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: What else did you do that day at that particular spot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: How long did you spend in -- as an entire duration, how long did you spend at that particular spot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: I don't know what to say. Probably half an hour, then we left again.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. That clarifies the previous question. What did you then do? You said that you left. Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: Afterwards I went to Prapaqan, to Tahir Zemaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Who is Tahir Zemaj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: At that time I knew he was a commander in the area of Peje, in Prapaqan village. I never knew him and I had never seen him before. He was a commander of the KLA in Prapaqan village, Peje municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Do you know where Zemaj is today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: I heard that he was killed. I don't know anything else about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. What about Prapaqan, where exactly is it? Could you give us an accurate description of its position.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: In fact, that was the only time I went there. I never went there again. I don't know what else I could tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Do you recall which village or villages you went through to get to Prapaqan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: I know that from the villages that I know, I passed through Gllogjan, Irzniq, and from Irzniq we took a road which I was not familiar with, and that road then took us to Prapaqan.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Who was giving you the directions to get to Prapaqan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: I was with a friend. He gave me the directions for this village, and he accompanied me up to Prapaqan.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Was that friend the same one who'd been with you at the canal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Could you give us his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Witness 21, what is his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: His name is -- but first, I apologise, I would like to ask you if this is something that is going out to the public or that is only for the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is also going to the public, unless Mr. Dutertre asks for private session and then -- or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it is entirely up to you, but I feel that the witness has some difficulty here. If he can state it in public session, then that would be acceptable, agreeable, to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You are -- we hear some hesitation in your voice whether you should give that name or not. Is there anything -- could you tell us the reason even if that should be done in private session, why you would rather not give the name in public. Perhaps we'll turn into private session and hear from the witness on the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may proceed, Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Witness 21, I'm putting this question to you, but it is true that the answers are given to the Court. So perhaps you could look to Your Honours rather than looking at me when you give the answer, because the answers are for the Court and also for Defence counsel as well. So person number 1 gave you the directions. When you went through Irzniq, did you go through check-point -- did you go through a check-point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: Only the check-point at Gllogjan, at the exit of Gllogjan, then we continued to Irzniq and to some other villages that I don't know, and we arrived finally in Prapaqan.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Did you note the presence of KLA soldiers when you were on your way to Prapaqan; and if so, where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: I did see soldiers in villages, but I don't know those villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And in the village of Irzniq?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: How did you know that these were KLA soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: Some of them had uniforms, KLA uniforms. So we spoke with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Could you describe those uniforms that you're referring to as KLA uniforms.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: Those were the KLA uniforms. I don't know how I should describe them. These were military uniforms, grass green. There were some with mixture of colours, camouflaged, green grass colour with -- mixed with other colours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Were they wearing any insignia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: Only the KLA military insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: You said that you spoke to them. To whom precisely did you speak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: I don't know them. We spoke to some, but I don't know those persons, who they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: What was the subject of your conversation? What did you say to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: These were informal chats, things that you usually talk about with friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Fine. Once you got to Prapaqan, who did you see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: In Prapaqan we met with Tahir Zemaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And what did you say to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: I asked him to help me find (redacted). I informed him -- I gave him some information about some military [as interpreted] movements. He said to me that he will help me find them and that if they had entered KLA territory, he would do his best to find them, dead or alive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Dutertre, I asked for a -- for striking out a couple of words. I take it that you understand what it is, and would you please consider carefully when it will be needed to go into private session. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Line 25 should read "their movement," not "military movement."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's on the record. Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Witness 21, what did you do afterwards once you had that discussion with Tahir Zemaj?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And perhaps I -- Witness 21, if you are referring to missing persons, just say "missing persons" instead of giving further details which might enable other persons to find out who you are. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: What did you do once you had that conversation with Tahir Zemaj, Witness 21?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: After this conversation, we returned to Dubrave at friend number 1's place, and then we agreed to meet the next day. We met the next day again.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Where did you meet the next day, at what location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: In the village of my friend, where his house was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: I'm going to put a question, but this will bring up the problem that we had previously. Were there other persons with you when you met person number 1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/21
utterances.text: Yes. There was another friend, who is also related to me, he is

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. After conversation with my colleague Mr. Emmerson and having watched the way the testimony has been proceeding, I think that it's going to get to a point of being really highly unworkable in terms of dealing with the various people that we're talking about, and perhaps it would be best to just do the whole thing in closed session and afterwards --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: See whether there are portions that could be made public without --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. Because it's just becoming -- I think it's realistically just becoming too cumbersome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Dutertre, I take it there's no objection against this suggestion. We'll then turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I would however --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I do, however, maintain my objection to proceeding along the basis of letting these names not being public; however, understanding the Chamber's ruling I would make this as a suggestion because this is becoming much too cumbersome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just further to that, can I indicate that it is going to become essential for Your Honours to have a grasp of who is who and where is where in the course of cross-examination of this witness. There are two portions of his evidence which on their face would not necessarily need to be in private session. One, he has already dealt with, that is to say, the description of what it was he saw and where he saw it at the time of his first visit to the canal; and the second is the description of what he saw and where he saw it at the time of his second visit to the canal. All companions and associations along the way fall into the category that Your Honours have indicated. So if we are to move into open session, those might be the two areas where it could be dealt with without any risk at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Dutertre, I -- let me just first ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre, we'll turn into private session, and you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're not yet in private session for unknown reasons, but ... I wonder why we are not in private session where there seems to be some turmoil in the technical booth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There seems to be a technical problem as far as private and public session is concerned; for that reason, the Chamber would like to have a break a little bit earlier than usual. We will have a break until five minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue I would like to deal with a few procedural matters. The Chamber has invited the parties to make further submissions on Witness 8. The question was deadline and whether it would be simultaneously or sequential --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just before Your Honour gives an indication, I had an opportunity to discuss this very briefly with Mr. Kearney earlier this afternoon. I don't know whether he has anything he would want to add to his position.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't, except that my colleague had suggested the fact that we -- since we hadn't received word from the Trial Chambers about a scheduling that would take -- that the Prosecution take the matter under submission as to how it wants to proceed with this witness. We had talked about that briefly. We hadn't come to a conclusion, frankly. We put ourselves in the Trial Chambers' hands. Does the Court have a thought as to when it wants a submission by the parties to be made?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think we asked for submissions, of course if the parties discuss the matter first, there's nothing against that, but not -- the submissions, we would like to receive them not later than this Friday. This gives you a bit of time to further discuss the matter, and since in the first round this is not a promise that there will be any second round, but at least the submissions now to be made can be sequential. That means that if the Prosecution has made its submissions by this Friday, that the Defence will have until after the weekend. So you could work on it already, but it will be sequential. This is, again, also not a promise that if there will be a next round that it will be sequential again. That is one. Then ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The next issue is that the Chamber would like to deliver its decision in relation to an oral -- an application for protective measures for Witness 60. The reasons for the Chamber's prior decision granting protective measures for Witness 60 are the following. On the 30th of March, 2007 --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I do apologise for rising to my feet. It may be that we are at cross-purposes, but Witness 60 on our list is a forensic expert who's never had protective measures. I think there may be some --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then there may be -- sometimes we have two numberings --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Or three sometimes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- numbers appear -- and if these had been mixed up, then I'll first verify that before I issue any decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll leave that then for the time being and it could be dealt with -- would be the number of in accordance with the list of how the witness would appear before this Court. Then--

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Whenever Your Honour has a moment, there are two short procedural matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I have another. I'll give you an opportunity to -- on the 23rd of March of this year the Chamber has requested the Office of the Prosecution to provide information on the security situation concerning witnesses in Kosovo and has requested the Defence to provide the information it deems relevant. On the 24th of March the Chamber has requested to be informed by the parties if no agreement on the matter could be reached, because that was suggested that stipulations could be made. On the 28th of March, the Office of the Prosecution has sent a letter to the Legal Officer with an annex listing materials relevant to witness security in Kosovo. That means that there's no agreement reached. And the Chamber would like to receive submissions as it initially asked for to the parties. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I formally and on the record indicate our position as far as the Haradinaj Defence team is concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Our position is that in respect to any witness falling within the second category, that is to say a witness of whom there is no evidence of threats, that if in respect of any such witness the first two of the three criteria laid down in the Trial Chamber's ruling are met, we will not oppose protective measures in those circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. We'll consider that. But of course, then the Chamber would also like to know, not necessarily immediately, whether the other Defence teams would take a similar position. But perhaps you take your time, read again what Mr. Emmerson said. It's always wise to read his words again and then inform the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: My -- I think that's been my inclination also, but I agree with you, it is always wise to read the words again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey, do you belong to the group of wise men who start reading before talking?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I shall take my cue from you, Your Honour, I think it is a sensible precaution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. We'll hear then from you and see to what extent -- that of course is the issue, to what extent this has any influence on our request to be fed with further information on the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, is this to be a Friday submission as well, this next submission that you're asking for?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, as a matter of fact, first we'll hear tomorrow morning -- tomorrow in the afternoon, I take it from other Defence counsel whether they take a similar position as Mr. Emmerson did. And after that, the Chamber will indicate whether under those circumstances it would still need in order to deal with further applications for protective measures. Yes. Then these were the issues at this moment. Then we could -- yes, Mr. Emmerson. Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Since we are -- we're dealing with procedural issues at this stage, may I just mention two. The next witness to be called in sequence is the witness who is planned to give evidence by videolink on Wednesday. We received just a few moments ago a very, very brief one-sided bullet-point notes arising from a proofing session that took place on the 12th of March for an hour and a half or thereabouts. And may I, through the Trial Chamber, or rather, on the record request a fuller record of that briefing session, that proofing session than five or six bullet-points for what was obviously a lengthy discussion in respect of that witness. Secondly, in terms of procedure, I'm not sure how much longer Mr. Dutertre's likely to be with the present witness. Cross-examination of this witness is likely to take a little time. One of the things that I'm anxious about is not to create -- or for a situation not to arise later in the week in which pressure is placed on the time that has been set aside for Colonel Crosland's evidence. And he, as I understand it, is available for two days. I've indicated some time ago in writing that he is a witness who I would expect to, with the Trial Chamber's permission, to be cross-examining for some considerable period of time. Now, we have received from the Prosecution in respect of Colonel Crosland a Rule 92 ter application in respect of a transcript of his evidence as --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- as given in the Limaj trial. But we've also received notification that the Prosecution intends to serve upon the Defence a 92 ter statement in respect of that witness, and that, presumably, is a statement that emerges from the proofing session Mr. Re conducted in London some weeks ago, and I have been requesting now for two weeks or so copies of any proofing notes or statements to have arisen from the session that took place with Colonel Crosland. I have received nothing, and I'm anxious that priority be given to the provision to the Defence of the 92 ter statement, the motion, and the proofing notes so that this is -- witness can be properly prepared. But I'm also anxious that we don't find ourselves in a situation that -- given that we have to do a videolink on Wednesday, that there may be pressure put on Colonel Crosland's evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Who's going to answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will. I find myself at a somewhat of a disadvantage. Neither one of these witnesses, Colonel Crosland or the videolink witness belong to Mr. Dutertre or myself. As soon as court breaks this evening, I will talk to both Mr. Re and Mr. Di Fazio about both the issues that Mr. Emmerson has raised and we will contact the Defence informally before court tomorrow and try and work these matters out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And if there are any major problems of which the parties would think it would be advantageous the Chamber to be aware of it, then the Judges of the Chamber are tomorrow morning in as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the first request, Mr. Emmerson, is clearly on the record. I don't think that we have to spend much time on it at this very moment. We'll then move again into private session under the circumstances. Mr. Dutertre, could you inform us about how much time you'd still need.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Rather difficult to say, Your Honour. I am trying to adapt myself to what the Defence has requested, which is why I had added some photos that I hadn't selected to begin with, and obviously it will take some time to show each of them. But I would say that I need roughly another hour with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This being said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Dutertre, the witness was scheduled for one hour and a half; we've spent now three hours. And even if there were quite a lot of suggestions made to speed up, and that of course in itself takes some time as well, you certainly couldn't say that that was one hour and a half. I mean, if we have to say -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, unless I'm mistaken, according to the timetable I have before me, it was foreseen that three and a half hours be granted for this witness. This is on line -- yes, there's confusion with the numbering -- 21. But from the left-hand column, the far left, there's a number 24 which corresponds to Witness 21, and that gives us three and a half hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll have to check in the preparation. For this session we had, at least in my preparatory work - and I do not always take all the sources with me - but it says estimated time for examination-in-chief: One hour and a half. But we'll check whether there's any -- any mistake there. If so, then of course I apologise for making you nervous.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar just gives me now the list filed on the 2nd of March which indicates for Witness 21 three and a half hours. So to the extent that I made a mistake there, I hope you'll accept my apologies then, Mr. Dutertre. Let the witness -- yes. I think we are not yet in private session. We should turn into private session now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 17th day of April, 2007, at 2.15 p.m. 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.00 p.m.,
